tagline: Africa's biggest city — an island-and-lagoon megacity running on hustle, Afrobeats, jollof rice and traffic locals call 'go-slow'.
overview: Lagos is Africa's largest city and its loudest — an estimated 16-plus million people spread across islands, lagoons and mainland suburbs linked by causeways and the famous 'go-slow' traffic jams.

The city runs on hustle and sound: Afrobeats was born here, Nollywood turns out thousands of films a year, and the markets — Balogun's fabric maze, the Lekki craft market — sell everything. At night the mainland's live-music bars and Victoria Island's clubs compete for the crowd.

Speed's 2025 Africa stop streamed from Lagos to ecstatic crowds — one of the biggest turnouts of the trip. Visitors get Kalakuta (Fela Kuti's house-museum), Africa's longest canopy walkway at Lekki Conservation Centre, and boat escapes to Tarkwa Bay.

funFacts.title: AFRICA'S BIGGEST CITY
funFacts.text: Estimates pass 16 million — the continent's largest urban area, still growing fast.

funFacts.title: AFROBEATS' BIRTHPLACE
funFacts.text: Fela Kuti's Lagos Shrine invented Afrobeat; today's Afrobeats stars took it global.

funFacts.title: THE CITY OF ISLANDS
funFacts.text: Victoria Island, Ikoyi and Lagos Island connect by bridges over the lagoon.

funFacts.title: NOLLYWOOD'S ENGINE
funFacts.text: Nigeria's film industry — one of the world's largest by output — is headquartered here.

funFacts.title: THE GO-SLOW
funFacts.text: Traffic jams are so famous they have a local name — pack snacks for the commute.

funFacts.title: FELA'S HOUSE

funFacts.title: THE JOLLOF WAR

funFacts.title: THE FLOATING SCHOOL
funFacts.text: Makoko's stilt village on the lagoon built a famous floating school.
